result: {"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom body line of the fish, stroke 2, which forms the whole lower outline from the nose to the tail fork. That is a large part of what makes the shape read as a fish. The fish was fully connected, and all 118 of 118 dominoes fall from the start. Execution: I traced stroke 2 in several batches, then stood one domino back up. After that I switched to inspection and ran six close checks on the joints and the chain between 1:30 and 5:15. I flagged that the top run went pale after the first bend, and I confirmed when it went dark all the way through, which cleared Omar and Jack to build the tail pieces. I also warned that sharp tail tips were the likeliest place for a stall. Collaboration: I kept the table informed about the state of the chain, including which pieces were connected and when it was safe to move on. I backed the decision that Omar's tail tip should end near the other line instead of joining it, which avoided a risky joint. I stayed out of other people's work areas so we didn't bump each other. Leadership: I took the verification role without being asked and kept it going for the whole build. I gave clear go-ahead signals on the top run and the tail pieces, and I helped move the team to a hands-off state well before the push. The result is a clean, connected fish outline that a judge should be able to recognise. I believe my part was one of the central pieces, covering the bottom line and the connection checks.", "my_share_percent": 30}
